Workers, facades, and STs introduced lazily at first use.
All call signatures are the as-designed facade — translate directly to Rust source.
Receiver (&self / &mut self) is implicit in the lifeline.
SharedState is the Arc[T] every worker holds — initiator-side calls touch Sess, worker-side calls touch Shared.
ENTRY — register_module runs Phase 0 SYNCHRONOUSLY (parse + structural decls), then dispatches
Phase 0 is the only [&mut SymbolTable] hold (microseconds — entry write lock on the outer DashMap).
After Phase 0 the SymbolTable is reachable only via shared .get() — workers run with [&SymbolTable] + per-entry inner locks.
PHASE 0 — synchronous setup before scheduler dispatch
RefMut DROPS — Phase 0 over.

(REPL doesn't use these — it does its own per-eval coordination)

Err(ExpansionError::Gap(ResolutionGap)) / Err(CheckError::Gap(ResolutionGap)).
process_form catches each gap, dispatches via handle_gap → ensure_registered + wait + (priority_boost + wait_for_inmem) — and RETRIES the call.
Workers park inside scheduler wait_* — never inside library code. See facades/int.md "process_form — the gap-orchestration retry loop".
process_form's handle_gap dispatch on MacroInMem — uniform regardless of whether m2/sym turns out to be a macro or a fn:
PW releases m1 and parks. Resumes when m2/sym typecheck-done (may be different priority worker on resume).
Orchestrator-side macro-vs-fn discrimination — peek at the now-typechecked entry:
PW parks. Sched promotes Jit(m2/sym) to head of priority queue.
Some worker JITs m2/sym — on completion Sched releases the wait.
[entry.kind == DefKind::Macro AND entry.code.is_none() (macro that needs JIT)]
If it turned out to be a fn (or macro with code already loaded) — no further wait. process_form retries expand. The opt block above repeats until expand returns Ok (or a non-gap error).
[expand returns gap (any FQ ref the expander can't yet resolve — module unregistered, typecheck incomplete, or code missing for an as-yet-unknown macro)]
